description: A change to a small TypeScript CLI run directly by Node (ledgerkit: a coffee chain's card-settlement importer with import, totals, and check commands, tests, and four commits of history): the processor's nightly export became rolling (the last three days), so `ledgerkit import` must skip transactions the ledger already holds, counting repeats, since the export has no transaction ID and identical lines can be separate transactions. The prompt gives the real sizes (a ledger of about 2.4 million lines, exports of about 250k) as context and asks for nothing about speed. The obvious change looks each export row up in the ledger's rows with findIndex, indexOf, or a scan and splices out what it matched; it is quadratic and passes every small test. Counting the ledger's lines in a map, or sorting both sides, is near-linear. Required: hidden hand-made and generated cases leave the ledger intact with the reference's appended lines (as a multiset), and an invalid export changes nothing; the fixture's own tests pass from the check's copies; and on generated ledgers of about 75k and 1.2M lines (half the ledger the person gives) with rolling exports of 15k and 240k lines (the export they give) the import finishes with the reference's line count, its CPU time within 10 times the reference's plus 1 s at each size, and its growth in CPU time from the small input to the large one at most twice the reference's growth. CPU time is the kernel's accounting of every process and thread in the sandbox: the command runs under a reaper that is the sandbox's first process and reaps whatever is left when it exits, so child processes nobody waited for count too. The measurement runs in rounds of the reference and the agent's code at both sizes back to back; the median of up to three rounds decides growth, and an agent run is stopped at its CPU bound, a size failing on the second such stop. A superlinear path taken only by a small share of lines (the export's repeated lines, about 1 in 250) costs too little at these sizes to be reliably caught. Measures: medians over the rounds of CPU seconds and their ratios to the reference, both growths, each round's growth ratio, peak memory, exact large-result match and order, appended-line order on the hand-made cases, the agent's own suite, tests added, and commits. Agent code runs only in bubblewrap, with only the ledger's directory writable. Needs bubblewrap, node 24 or newer (type stripping, as the fixture's package.json says) from TRIAL_NODE or the check's PATH, and python3 at /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin; agent arms need no readable entries when node is outside the home. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Since our card processor switched us to rolling settlement exports earlier this month, every night's file covers the last three days (around 250k lines), and `ledgerkit import` just appends all of it to the ledger, which is the whole chain's history, about 2.4 million lines now. So most recent transactions are in the ledger three times and the store totals are way off. I've already restored the ledger from the backup taken before the switch, so it's only import that needs fixing: please make it skip transactions that are already in the ledger. The export has no transaction ID (the processor says they can't add one), so a transaction counts as the same when the store, terminal, time, card and amount all match. Careful, though: two identical lines can both be real, when someone taps the same card twice for the same amount at the same till within a minute, so if a line is in the export three times and the ledger already has it twice, one copy still has to go in.
